summary:
FMLink, a partner of the International Federation of Healthcare Engineering (IFHE), promotes the co-located IFHE 29th World Congress and Healthcare Design (HCD) Conference + Expo, held October 17-20, 2026 at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center in New Orleans. The article positions the event as the premier gathering for hospital facility executives and planners, noting dedicated facility management tracks plus IFHE programming that spans healthcare facility design, construction, engineering, operations and real estate management.

The IFHE World Congress is hosted by the Association of Medical Facility Professionals (AMFP), the U.S. representative to IFHE, in partnership with Emerald, the events and content parent company of HCD. IFHE membership spans more than 35 countries, which the piece says creates potential for diverse international perspectives at a U.S. event. This is the first time the two events share a single venue, described as a unified platform connecting professionals who design and build healthcare environments with those who operate them.

All registration pass types include IFHE sessions, but access to the full HCD program of 110+ sessions requires the IFHE + HCD Full Conference Pass. More than 100 educational sessions are offered, with AIA, IDCEC, EDAC and nursing learning units available. Tracks include Advancements in Evidence-Based Design Research, Behavioral Health Practices, Technology & Innovation, and Clinical Perspectives. Show features include networking lounges, the OM Seating hosted HCD Power Lounge, facility tours, keynotes, an exhibit hall, and a $10,000 cash giveaway.

The piece also details the Nightingale Awards, presented by Healthcare Design magazine in partnership with the HCD Conference + Expo, recognizing product design and innovation contributing to healing. A jury of healthcare design professionals and facility managers reviews entries digitally then visits exhibitor booths before the expo hall opens. Regular entry deadline is Aug. 31 ($695); late entry deadline is Sept. 28 ($795). The awards are named for Florence Nightingale.

FMLink links to prior articles on capital investment strategies, project team trust, medical campus construction, AI-enabled hospital efficiency and healthcare security.
